#3647. GTA 6 launch knocked Call of Duty's daily players down 42 percent, Alinea estimates

Grand Theft Auto 6's launch took a big bite out of Call of Duty’s player base, according to new estimates from Alinea Analytics, and four days on, it still hasn't recovered.

Writing in Alinea's newsletter, Rhys Elliott said Call of Duty HQ's daily active users (DAUs) across PlayStation, Xbox, and Steam fell 42 percent when GTA 6 launched on 19th November, dropping from an average of 7.5 million to 4.4 million. On PlayStation, which Elliott describes as "CoD's main platform", the drop was 44 percent.

"Sadly, CoD has barely bounced back after four days," Elliott wrote. "It's still down 41% from its baseline."

Fortnite and FC 27 took a hit too, but both are already recovering. Fortnite's DAUs on PlayStation and Xbox fell 28 percent, from 17.8 million to 12.8 million, but by the end of the weekend it had clawed its way back to 19 percent below its baseline.

Epic is also holding a live event to close out the current season on 5th December, which Elliott says the studio "hopes will pull players back after they’ve polished off GTA 6’s story".

FC 27's DAUs dropped by around 27 percent, from 5.9 million to 4.3 million, and it's already back within 20 percent of its baseline.

GTA 6's launch hit Call of Duty HARD (@alineaanalytics estimates).COD HQ's daily active users across PlayStation, Xbox, and Steam are down 42% from an average of 7.5M DAUs to 4.4M. On PlayStation – CoD’s main platform – Call of Duty took a 44% hit. Sadly, CoD has barely bounced… pic.twitter.com/XLa6N9TBfr

According to Alinea, of those who'd played GTA 6 by the end of its launch weekend, 29 percent had also played Fortnite this month, 16 percent had played Call of Duty HQ, and 11 percent had played FC 27.

Elliott said the pattern is largely what Alinea had predicted: the big live service games took an instant hit from GTA, but bounced back "because they're ingrained habits". Call of Duty is "the outlier here", he added, "and Xbox should - candidly - be worried about one of its premier franchises".

Elliott also points out that all of this is the impact of GTA 6's single-player mode. He expects its online component and PC port to arrive "some time next year", and when they do, he says, "the bounce back will not be so obtainable".

Alinea also estimates that GTA 6 has sold 44.9 million copies and made more than $4 billion since launch.

GTA 6 launched on Thursday, 19th November, for PS5 and Xbox Series X/S. While it's the biggest entertainment launch of all time, selling 32.5 million pre-release copies and making $3.79 billion by the end of its first day, you wouldn't know it from its Metacritic user score, as players review bomb it over its limited FPS and purported "woke" agenda.

Eurogamer called GTA 6 an open world of "awe, minute detail and impossible scale" in our five-star GTA 6 review. If you need help getting through the game now that it's here, you can check out Eurogamer's Grand Theft Auto 6 walkthrough and a breakdown of our Grand Theft Auto 6 cheats.

#3645. The Witcher 3 Remastered's latest patch takes aim at mods nicking all of Geralt's possessions, disappearing buildings and an outbreak of "overly bright red" NPC leg areas

Catronia's not the only plague the Northern Realms need fear, it seems

The Witcher 3 Remastered continues to recieve tweaks ahead of the Songs of the Past expansion arriving next year to whisk Gerry from the River off on a fresh adventure. Following some bloomin' improvements in October, its latest patch does a bunch of skill and mutation balancing, alongside further technical tweaks and fixes for some funky bugs.

"Fixed an issue where Reforging the Mastercrafted or Grandmaster Feline armor gave Geralt an unusual hairstyle," reads the first of numerous notes in the visual section of patch 5.02's notes about weird stuff happening to Gerry's luscious mane. "Fixed an issue where Geralt could become bald after enabling HairWorks on PC or Xbox Play Anywhere and then continuing the game on Xbox via Cross Progression," reads another that sounds slightly more serious. "Fixed an issue where growing a beard with the Rabble-rouser hairstyle made Geralt's head invisible," reads a third, which takes the cake.

There've also been instances of Gerry or NPCs missing their faces or "other body parts". The NPCs, bless them, have also had to deal with contracting "overly bright red areas on their legs" when moving through crowds. Oh, and a building near Novigrad's docks has been cheeklily disappearing whenever Geralt gets close to it. One would assume it's just a bit shy, though that's a tough thing to be when your location means people embarking and disembarking from ships are constantly walking past. To be honest, it also sounds like it could have been adapted into an extra contract for Gerry if CD Projekt had fancied. The studio have also "fixed an issue where installing and uninstalling mods could cause merchants' inventories, Geralt's inventory and storage to be emptied".

Beyond the giggle-worthy bug fixes, the most consequential aspect of the patch to my eye will likely be the tweaks to the power of certain skills and mutations, which folks may well be testing out if they're trying to settle on a new build before Songs of the Past. Those tweaks are as follows:

Generally speaking, sign-heavy Gerry builds look like they'll be most acutely affected and be less effective following this patch. I typically only rely on Quen for a bit of shielding, because I'm an unimaginative monster slayer, so I'm not sure I'll notice it too much, but if you really make the most of your magical abilities it might hit your Gerry pretty hard.

It's worth skimming through the full notes if you've time, which also contain a few PC-specific fixes and tweaks. Starting a Hearts of Stone or Blood and Wine-only playthrough on Steam Deck should no longer lead to long load times, for example, while there've been some improvements made to path tracing and ray reconstruction .

#3644. You can expect a similar leap between The Witcher 3 and The Witcher 4 as there is between GTA 5 and GTA 6, CD Projekt Red says

CD Projekt Red has said people can expect a similar qualitative and technological leap from The Witcher 3 to The Witcher 4 as has been witnessed between Grand Theft Auto 5 and Grand Theft Auto 6.

CDPR joint-CEO Michał Nowakowski made the remark during a Q3 earnings call this afternoon, during which he and CDPR faced a handful of questions related to GTA 6.

"First of all, obviously this is a call about us, not about Rockstar," Nowakowski began by saying, "but I do understand the connection here. Having said that, I'm not going to make a deep-dive and a full-blown review of GTA 5 versus GTA 6. But of course we did look at the game, we did see the differences.

"We believe there's going to be a comparable leap between The Witcher 3 and The Witcher 4 - I think so, yes. It's been 11 years, we are working on The Witcher 4 to make it significantly better looking and improved in terms of pretty much every possible facet of the game, so yes you should expect us to make a much bigger jump between Witcher 3 and Witcher 4."

Another question was about whether GTA 6 had affected development plans for The Witcher 4 and Cyberpunk 2 - a question well-timed after Cyberpunk 2 creative director Igor Sarzynski joked at the weekend that "Cyberpunk 2 is cancelled" because of how impressive GTA 6 is.

"Is seeing GTA 6 launch making us make the games more expensive?" said Nowakowski. "We have certain ambitions when it comes to Witcher [4] and Cyberpunk 2; they have not changed when it comes to GTA 6. If anything happened as a result of GTA 6, it's [that it's] always great to see games like that because they show you how much cool stuff can be done, and that's for sure an inspiration in many ways for our developers."

Specifically in terms of budget, Nowakowski said nothing had changed, and also echoed a point made earlier this year when he said Witcher 4 and Cyberpunk 2 are "not budget-driven developments".

"I'm not saying we don't care about the budgets: we do, and I'm pretty sure [Rockstar] did as well. But you cannot make games like that having in mind 'this is the fixed number of money I want to spend and that's it, otherwise I'm gone'," he said.

"They're ambition-driven developments and money's important - the budgets are not indefinite, that's not what we're saying. But the philosophy is like I said, and honestly that philosophy has not changed for us because of GTA 6's release; it has just always been like that."

When asked whether the arrival of GTA 6 had impacted sales of The Witcher 3 and Cyberpunk 2077, Nowakowski answered "yes and no". "You do see a certain dip in engagement on the PlayStation and Xbox for sure," he said.

Statistics apparently show a drop of "at least" 25 percent in CDPR's players as they "engaged themselves with GTA 6". "But you do have to remember that a lot of our players are PC-based," Nowakowski pointed out. "GTA has not launched on PC; we have not seen any impact whatsoever on the PC sales or engagement. So it's a bit of a mixed answer.

"And also on the PS5 and Xbox, it's not like our sales came to zero," he added. "Some short impact, yes, on the consoles. Long-term, we do not really see that affecting ourselves in any material way in Q4."

Finally, the questioning turned to marketing, which Rockstar has shown can reach far and wide if you have the brand-power of GTA and some imagination. We've seen prestigious department stores like Selfridges taken over by Rockstar for GTA 6, trailers premiering on Netflix, Miami launch festivals - Rockstar's marketing department has gone all out.

CDPR is no stranger to grabbing headlines with glitzy actor hirings such as Keanu Reeves, but will Rockstar's approach to marketing GTA 6 push it a step further?

"The most important takeaway - I'm not sure if I'd call it a lesson because this is our playbook as well - is that if you want to reach a certain critical mass, you do have to get out of just the core gaming bubble, something we did in the past as well," Nowakowski said. "For sure, GTA 6 went there.

"If the underlying question was if we're going to repeat or copy-paste their playbook: no, for sure not. Our games are different and they require a certain different approach - we just do things differently than they do. But in terms of the ultimate effect, in terms of breaking out to the mass market awareness: this is for sure something we consider pivotal to whatever we're going to do with our marketing campaigns in the future."

CDPR's Q3 financial results were positive. The company made less money than this time last year, but the "fresh momentum" - as Nowakowski put it - provided to The Witcher 3 and Cyberpunk 2077 by the release of the Remastered edition of Witcher 3 and the Edgerunners anime series on Netflix, and associated game update, went a long way.

The Witcher 3 reached its highest concurrent player count on Steam as a result, and Cyberpunk 2077 reached its second highest concurrent player count, which represents serious staying power for both games so long after they were first released. And with Witcher 3 expansion Songs of the Past on track for 2027, and The Witcher 4 for 2028, the future is loaded.

Larian has a purer relationship with the audience

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

The industry's in a troubling position right now. Layoffs are widespread, triple-A budgets have ballooned, and it seems harder than ever to know what'll make a game stick. In the mind of one of the central devs on the Path of Exile series, Baldur's Gate 3 is a strong example of the kind of business model studios should aspire toward.

Chris Wilson, former lead designer on Path of Exile and co-founder of Grinding Gear Games, discussed the merits of Larian's approach with Destin on YouTube. "A like Baldur's Gate 3 is a great example of a very true game," he says.

"They made it, they had a good extended early access period for getting feedback without spoiling the game, and they released it in a sincere way," he explains. "Then, when given the opportunity to do more stuff for it, they said, actually, we want to make something else. That's cool, they'll make another thing, and that'll do well."

To his perception, "there's no manipulation there." Larian "got rewarded" appropriately and "everyone had a good time" in that transaction. "Sure, it's because it's an exceptionally good game," he adds. "But I think that a shift back to making games [like that] - it's less complicated, you can make more story-driven games. It doesn't have to be that everything is a live-service."

That's the million-dollar principle, really. Many games at the triple-A level simply don't need these features or mechanics, and Baldur's Gate 3 proves you can still have a close-to-one-to-one transaction between you and the player and be hugely successful.

Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 and the Final Fantasy 7 remake trilogy are further examples. Wilson admits he probably wouldn't have made Path of Exile if they couldn't do it with live-service aspects, but that's because they were integral to the vision.

"It's designed around a big economy with lots of players, which is why it's free-to-play," he says. "It was very much designed to be live-service from the start."

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more

The current problem is games are being released with online elements "because the spreadsheet says it'll make more money," and the game is "contorted out of its single-player true experience" to facilitate these elements.

It must be said, it is refreshing still to play something and not have any online components to worry about or consider. Some games should just be their own experiences, and we need more of them - even if my to-play pile continues growing.

#3642. The Steam Awards turn 10 with throwback categories and a Game of the Year Hall of Fame

Nominations for the 2026 Steam Awards are now open, and to mark the event's 10th anniversary, Valve has brought back some categories from years past and added a Hall of Fame.

You've got until 6pm UK (10am Pacific) on 30th November to nominate your favourite games of the year across 14 categories. Returning throwbacks include Just 5 More Minutes, Defies Description, and This is My Job Now, which recognises games that simulate mundane real-life jobs.

The new Hall of Fame category will appear when voting opens, and will let players choose their favourite from Steam's previous Game of the Year winners to crown the best game of the past decade.

Most categories are only open to games released on Steam since last year's Autumn Sale.

The exception is the Labo(u)r of Love award, which goes to older games that developers are still supporting with new content. Previous Labo(u)r of Love winners, including Warframe, Grand Theft Auto 5, Cyberpunk 2077, and Baldur's Gate 3, can't be nominated again.

Five finalists will be revealed in each category when voting opens alongside the Steam Winter Sale on 17th December. Voting closes at 10am Pacific on 2nd January, and the winners will be announced straight afterwards.

Nominating in at least one category also earns you the first level of Steam's Nomination Committee badge.

Earlier this month, Valve released a new Steam update that adds Steam Deck framerate data to a game's store page, giving potential buyers an indication of how well a game runs on the handheld.

#3641. Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine 2's latest updates introduces a Weekly Clash mode that shakes up PvP with some constricting modifiers

In as booming a monster truck rally commentator voice as you can imagine: ARE YOU READY TO GET DECIMATED??? Yes? Yippee! Because I've got some good news for you. The latest update for Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine 2 is here, appropriately dubbed the Decimation update, which adds in a new mode and more.

First up, that new mode! It's called Weekly Clash and it's for the competitive folks out there. "This new PvP shakes things up with the introduction of “Weekly Clash”, a new mode that brings unique new rules to Eternal War, like games restricted to a single class, a single weapon or even granting near-unlimited grenades," explains a Steam blog post. "Except more modifiers to be added in the future."

This update also introduces a new Chaos Siege sector, that new mode introduced last month, which adds in a "new playable sector bringing a renewed challenge between waves 11 and 15!" You'll also find six new heroic weapons in the armoury, like the omnissian axe, plasma incinerator and heavy bolter. This comes complete with some new heroic armour pieces, specifically four new helmets. On top of all of this, there's been a Vanguard rework: "Fight the enemies of Humanity with new ways to use your Grapnel Launcher! Attack cancellations, close-quarter kicks and a new Revenge mechanic make the Vanguard as bold and brutal as he’s ever been!"

Some other general tweaks have been made with this patch too. All PvP maps have seen the number and locations of ammo and equipment pickups adjusted, and conditions for the spawn position swap system have been improved. A level lock for the Absolute Siege and Absolute Stratagems mode has also been added; "The difficulty will be accessible to Classes that have reached level 25 or achieved Prestige at least once." And you'll also find that loading times and general connectivity should be a bit better!

The Nathan Fielder/Lance Oppenheim co-directed hit documentary You Can See Everything, which has done huge box office numbers on the 2026 movie schedule, does a very deep dive into Elizabeth Holmes after Theranos. Now, everyone from former employees to psychologists is weighing in on Holmes both before and after her fraud convictions led to a long prison sentence that she is currently serving in Texas. Recently, one of Holmes’ assistants, Aria Marinelli, from the early days of Theranos, appeared on the Assistants vs. Agents podcast and spoke about a few red flags she saw in her short time working for the disgraced CEO.

Marinelli worked for Holmes at Theranos in 2009, which lands right in the middle of the company’s history, which was founded in 2003 and collapsed in 2016 before going completely out of business in 2018. Holmes went to prison in 2023. Marinelli wasn’t at the company long, by the sound of things, but did work directly for Holmes in her time with the Silicon Valley startup that promised big things with what we now know was a completely fraudulent blood-testing machine (a machine Marinelli says she never even laid eyes on until seeing You Can See Everything).

In the interview, she highlights a few things that made her question whether she wanted to be part of the company and if what they were doing was legitimate. According to Marinelli, the suspicions started even before she accepted the job, as she explained:

I went and looked through old emails just to see if I was remembering correctly, and it turns out I was. So this is [an email to] a mentor of mine. I said: ‘It's looking like I have to get Theranos an answer tomorrow regarding their offer. It expires at COB, and they've already extended it once. I'm very hesitant to accept because the work and the work environment are really not my ideal next step. Something about it doesn't sit right, I guess.’

She went on to explain that pretty early on, there was never a lot of talk about what the company was trying to do with the machine. In typical Silicon Valley style, according to Marinelli, most of the talk was about stock shares, IPOs, and how much money they could all make. That was something else that didn’t sit right with her.

Not only did Marinelli never see the now-infamous device, but she never saw a blood testing lab at all and was worried that despite famous names on the board of directors, there seemed to be no one with medical knowledge. That also raised concerns for her, as she explained:

The biggest thing was that there was no lab. So I had noticed that there were no doctors on the board, and that's, again, been talked about ad nauseam, but I was willing to dismiss that as maybe they were just getting started, right? And I remember just being told, ‘Oh, it's off-site,’ but I never saw anybody in that time frame that was working in a lab or that was from that lab.

The final straw for Marinelli was when she was tasked with tracking down one of the company’s machines from the Army, which was supposedly testing it. Through multiple emails and phone calls, she seemed to be a wild goose chase, with everyone pointing to other people, and no one knowing where the device actually was. Marinelli told host Warner Bailey:

Everyone [at Theranos] is very secretive, very, you know, shielded in how they're speaking about this thing. I doubt they would just ship it off to someone and not have them have a concerted program around testing it.  So that, to me, was kind of the last flag that I was willing to put up with.

Marinelli also gave her honest impression of Holmes, and it wasn’t all negative, but she did mention that she thought The Dropout, the series starring Amanda Seyfried that can be seen with a Hulu subscription, is a fair portrayal of Holmes as Marinelli knew her. She also praised You Can See Everything and seems to have real sympathy for Holmes, saying, “everyone has to lie at that level.”

One of the many interesting and brilliant things about You Can See Everything is that everyone sees something different in it, including the people who worked for Holmes and Theranos, and I don’t think this is the last time we’ll hear from people who worked with her and knew her. Especially as this movie continues to get Oscar buzz and will continue to be in the cultural zeitgeist for some time.

#3639. Lords of the Fallen 2 delayed to April 2027, exact release date coming next month

Lords of the Fallen 2 will now launch in April 2027, and we'll find out exactly when next month.

The news came via a short post on X from CI Games founder and CEO Marek Tyminski. "Lords of the Fallen II: April 2027," he wrote. "Exact date in December."

That means the Soulslike sequel has slipped again. Back in June, CI Games pushed Lords of the Fallen 2 into a Q1 2027 release window, saying the extra time would let the team refine the game and keep it clear of "a highly competitive holiday period". That was a delay in itself, as when CI Games and Epic ended the game's PC exclusivity deal in May, it was still targeting a 2026 release.

Last month, CI Games secured a €28.6 million (around $32 million) loan to complete production and release Lords of the Fallen 2, as well as refinance its existing bank debt, according to a stock exchange filing. The loan matures on 31st August 2027, and, as reported at the time, CI Games will self-publish the game and expects to repay the loan through its sales.

Lords of the Fallen II: April 2027. Exact date in December. pic.twitter.com/yYaevDqaxe

Lords of the Fallen 2 is coming to PS5, Xbox Series X/S, Nintendo Switch 2, and PC via Steam and the Epic Games Store.

Following its announcement in 2025 and a look at gameplay during that year's The Game Awards, Lords of the Fallen 2 - which is technically the series' third game if we don't ignore the fact it was rebooted - had been steadily marching towards an unspecified 2026 launch. On PC, the plan was for it to be an Epic Games Store exclusive, but that's no longer happening after we learned CI Games - developer and sole owner of the IP - is now free from the multi-year exclusivity deal with Epic Games.

The sequel has also been at the centre of heated conversations following CI Games founder and CEO Marek Tyminski's comments regarding "political correctness" and "real player feedback". The studio also raised eyebrows recently by announcing more revealing armour sets for female characters in Lords of the Fallen 2, for instance, compared to its previous project.

Eurogamer gave the rebooted Lords of the Fallen two stars, calling it "a perfectly acceptable Soulslike that's often fun to play and offers the same satisfaction at overcoming adversity", but one let down by "Soulslike clichés and performance woes".

I've lost count of how many times I've settled down to play a brand-new game on Steam, only to be smacked in the face with a giant popup telling me to "Grab a controller and kick back!" instead of using my humble mouse and keyboard.

Thankfully for me I live in a multi-platform household, meaning a controller is never far out of reach. But I've also got staunch PC pals without a pad to pick up and who, rightly enough, don't want to fork out the kinda cash that PlayStation's DualSense or the Xbox controller require.

But I'm a firm believer that a good controller is a must-have tool in a PC gamer's repertoire these days, and we needn't immediately seek out the big names when it comes to a comfortable, robust gamepad. Tons of budget-friendly options have popped up on the market over the years, and while some of them are admittedly pretty naff there are also a bunch of great controllers that won't break the bank.

In fact, I've got three of 'em for under $25 for you right here. That's a third of the price of a DualSense controller! While they don't come with fancy haptics and adaptive triggers, they do offer stick-drift resistant, low-latency gaming. Which, as fun as the bells as whistles can be, are really the most important bits.

A new and improved version of the original Nova Lite, the Nova Lite 2 has Hall effect everything, 1000 Hz polling, and trigger locks. It even has a mechanical D-pad, which is absurd for the money, really.

Key specs: Wireless (Bluetooth and 2.4 GHz) | Asymmetric | Hall effect

Out of the three choices, our pad professional James Bentley tells me he likes the GameSir Nova Lite 2 the best, currently going for $23 at Walmart. It boasts comfort, decent polling, and Hall effect—so much better protection against that pesky stick drift. It's also got our highest review score out of the bunch thanks to its affordability, mechanical d-pad, and choice of 2.4Ghz and Bluetooth.

It's not got great grip, however, and its budget is felt in the less-than-stellar plastic and rather simple software. But for the price you're paying? It's a great, basic choice for those who only need to reach for a controller occasionally.

We've already raved about Hall effect joysticks and how they spell the end for the dreaded stick drift. In this wireless gaming controller, they're a welcome feature, but this handful of gaming hardware packs a few quirky surprises too. For instance, there are extra bumper buttons.

Key specs: Hall effect sticks, triggers | 2.4G wireless | 19 h battery

Price check: Best Buy $21.99 (Black) | Walmart $29.99 (Purple)

But if you're someone who's accustomed to the likes of the Switch Pro controller, you might find the 8BitDo Ultimate 2C a better fit, currently going for $20 at Amazon. It's got a pretty similar shape, and also sports those beloved Hall effect joysticks. It does have a little bit of a mushy d-pad but hey, look at that lovely colourway!

Finally, if you're looking to spend as little as possible, the GameSir Nova Lite comes in as the cheapest option at a mere $18. It's got less mappable buttons than its successor thanks to no back paddles, and is overall a downgrade. For the extra four bucks I'd personally just go for the newer version, but if you're really looking to really squeeze every cent, it's certainly an option worth considering.

It's incredible to think you can spend so little and get a stick drift-resistant wireless controller that doesn't completely suck. Luckily for the GameSir Nova Lite, it does all of the above and manages to feel good and light in the hands, too.

Key specs: Wireless (Bluetooth and 2.4 GHz) | Asymmetric | Hall effect

#3637. HARK THE GHOUL is a Victorian gothic dungeon crawler RPG that features a trench-coat-wearing rat man who wants to sell you rats a la counterfeit watches

I'm a simple person. I see an anthropomorphic rat man who opens up his trench coat that is filled with regular rats in the same manner as one would with counterfeit watches in a trailer for a video game, I add it to my wishlist. There really isn't much I need in life, but that certainly fulfills those needs. And it's exactly what HARK THE GHOUL is offering, an action-adventure, dungeon crawler RPG set in a weird and nasty Victorian gothic city with an emphasis on free exploration.

Now, I appreciate not all of you will be as immediately convinced by trench coat wearing rat men, so let's have a deeper gander at the game together. Exploration really does seem to be the key thing here, not just in terms of going wherever you want, more or less when you want, but how you get about. For example, say there's an annoying gap you want to cross. Use a magical spell to summon a crate, then lob it in front of you, and cast some icey magic to freeze it into place, thereby creating a new platform for you to hop onto. Looks like nice and systemic stuff!

HARK THE GHOUL releases 👉JANUARY 21st, 2027!!!👈 Our action-adventure RPG built around freeform exploration lets you loose in a dark Victorian city full of secrets to uncover and ravenous monsters to defeat! Coming to Steam, Switch 1, Switch 2, PS5 and Xbox Series![image or embed]

This extends to the combat, which faces you against odd automatons, infected foes and nasty beasties. You can perform quite silly tricks like using your shovel to dig up a rock and chuck that at a baddie, or you can use your magic to conjure up an explosive crate which you then kick at an enemy, blasting it with a shotgun. It appears to almost be an RPG by way of the immersive sim; there's no correct way to go about the game, only the way you find most fun. Though maybe that's dredging up the debate around what an immersive sim is…

Either way, I'm just tickled pink by HARK THE GHOUL, which also pits you as a mothman-type figure who's just emerged from their cocoon. Delightful! And it just got a release date too: January 21st, 2027. That's only a couple of months away, obviously, but if you can't wait that long then there's a demo you can check out on Steam. Or, you know, just throw it a wishlist! Offering it some support either way seems like a nice idea.

#3636. Performance analysis reveals GTA 6 has a more stable frame-rate on Xbox Series X compared to PlayStation 5

If you don't own a PlayStation 5 Pro, the best way to play Grand Theft Auto 6 is reportedly on Xbox Series X. That's according to new performance analysis, which shows Microsoft's console is more consistent at maintaining the game's 30fps frame-rate target than the base PS5.

The findings come from the tech experts Digital Foundry, who published a big report covering all the technical similarities and differences between Sony and Microsoft's consoles.

Unsurprisingly, PS5 Pro is in the lead with no competition, as Xbox elected not to release a mid-generation upgrade for the Series console family. Sony's more powerful console delivers "the definitive console GTA 6 experience," according to Digital Foundry. The PS5 Pro has the most stable 30fps performance of all four consoles, and benefits from a sharper presentation at 4K thanks to Sony's PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR) image upscaler, which upscales the image from a 1440p base resolution.

It's when comparing the base consoles - Xbox Series X and PS5 - that things get a little more interesting. Both target a 30fps frame-rate and often maintain that target, but certain sections trigger drops. According to the report, those include sequences with busy crowds and fast vehicle traversal. In some cases, the drops can be as low as mid-to-high 20fps.

With that in mind, PS5 has "substantially more frequent" frame-rate drops compared to Series X. The Xbox console is also aided by its support for 120Hz Variable Refresh Rate (VRR), which helps smooth out small dips in the frame-rate.

"Ultimately, Series X is meaningfully better off," Digital Foundry concluded.

Despite the studio's close marketing alignment with PlayStation historically - to the point Xbox can't even say GTA 6 in certain posts about GTA 6 - this is not the first time a Rockstar game has run better or looked better on an Xbox console.

At Red Dead Redemption 2's launch in 2018, Digital Foundry hailed Xbox One X as the best place to play it, owing to - unsurprisingly - a more stable 30fps frame-rate and sharper visuals. Not much has changed in the past eight years on that front, then.

Given all the information we have today, including the lack of 60fps and 40fps modes on PS5 Pro, it's going to be really interesting to see the kind of PC specs required to achieve parity with console visuals at 60fps and beyond. If Rockstar doesn't get there first, modders are already working on porting GTA 6 to PC.

#3635. Capcom's sci-fi dinosaur shooter Exoprimal is shutting down next year

Sad news dinosaur lovers. Exoprimal - Capcom's third-person sci-fi shooter with a Jurassic twist - will be shutting down next year. With its closure, the game will no longer be playable, even for those who've got it downloaded.

In a new post to the official Exoprimal website, it's revealed the game will be shuttered on 29th September 2027, at 8am PDT across all regions. Until then, all Survival Passes (battle pass equivalents) are no longer available for purchase, with the game and all its DLC stripped from stores on 30th March.

If you do fancy hopping in for a bit to send off Exoprimal in style, you'll still be able to re-download the game after it's taken off stores if you originally downloaded the game in the past. Tragically, the game will no longer be playable at all once shuttered, as there's no offline support. As an always-online game that requires a constant internet connection, it'll be one for the history books, at least in an official capacity.

Exoprimal was an interesting game for certain. A spin on the popular hero shooter, the game blended staples from the genre with some fairly cool twists. For one, the PvE elements were immediately interesting: seeing waves of raptors race towards you and your allies was critical to its appeal. On top of that, the PvPvE elements where two teams would race to complete objectives was pretty neat, thanks in large part to a variety of enjoyable exosuits at your disposal.

Even so, the game never really caught on to the extent that its peers did. Many pointed to the premium price tag paired with in-game microtransactions as a core factor to this, believing it would be hard to convince someone to play the game over something like Overwatch, which was free. Still, it had nearly a million players soon after launch, with Capcom stating it expected the game to be profitable in a financial report following the game's release. Whether or not it actually was remains unclear.

With that in mind, pay some mind to the Exoprimal players who don't have too long left with their game of choice. All the Krieger players out there have my sympathies. All the Vigilant players do not.

Grabbing a Truffade Thrax in GTA 6 isn't too hard, but if you want Andrew Node's supercharged version, the true fastest car around, you'll need to complete a little collectible hunt. Before you start, it's worth noting that this special Truffade Thrax costs 70k to register when you steal it, though you can also sell it to Randy for 20k (not that I would recommend this as it's a unique car).

The first step is scanning ten No Flusher toilet graffiti stamps around Vice Beach, the east portion of Vice City, with your WAiNK It app. Each symbol is basically a little blue toilet. After that, you'll have to head to a secret lockup, and then you're on for stealing the car.

This first one is southeast of Nola - Ocean beach on the pavement on the west side of the road.

The second is east of Podium Sports - Ocean Beach, on the south side pavement of the road leading out onto the grass towards the beach.

This one is at the east end of the bridge leading from Vice Beach to Waxman Island, on the southern pavement. Also to the west of LTD Gas - Ocean Beach

This fourth one is east of Aural Expert and north of Venus Fitness, on the pavement at the side of the junction.

This one is on the pavement directly in front of Banana Hole Main Bar, east down the road from the previous one above.

This sixth one is on the sidewalk on the far west of the road running along the bottom of the huge park in Vice Beach.

This seventh is west of Podium Sports - Ocean Beach, down the road you can see with the roundabout at the end on the map.

The eighth is east down the road from Shorefront - Ocean Beach bank and south of Easy Electronics, on the pavement on the corner.

This ninth is north of Marshal's jewelry and northeast of Endzone - Washington Beach, at the east end of the big carpark bordering the beach.

On the right side of the northern road at the Oldby Island junction, directly opposite Ron Gas - Washington Beach.

After you've found all ten, Cal's conspiracy theory chat (which unlocks after the first) will go dark, before you get a separate message a little later giving you their hideout location. Head there, read the note to the right of the garage door, and then flip it around to get the code for the lock:

Inside you'll have a bunch of evidence pointing to Andrew Node's house on Starfish island, so examine it all and then you're ready to steal the car.

First off, Starfish Island is a gated community with security, so it's better to get a boat there. Head west from the hideout and steal a boat on the piers, then drive west across the water to the jetty of Andrew Node's house—it's the one on the southern side towards the centre, that looks like a backwards L.

Dock, head around the left side of the house to find a white garage on the right you can open up with Andrew Node's Truffade Thrax inside. You'll have to drive it off the island, but after that you can head to Randy and register it for 70k. Just make sure you have the garage space and the money before you steal the car.

#3633. Promising action-RPG, Showa American Story, has been delayed into late 2027 in order to feel "cohesive, responsive and complete" at launch

"The game's content is already completely finished".

Publisher 4Divinity and developer Nekcom Entertainment have announced that upcoming action-RPG Showa American Story will now launch on 28th October, 2027. This comes after various sites noticed a Steam page update that listed the game as launching in 2027, slipping from the previous, vague window that suggested the game would come out this year. The announcement was made on the developer's Twitter account.

"Hello everyone!" reads the message. "We finally have an official release date to share: Showa American Story will launch on 28th October, 2027. Reaching this milestone after five years of development means a lot to our entire team. With core game content now complete, we're dedicating our full focus to polishing and optimizing the experience so that when you step into Showa American Story, it feels cohesive, responsive, and complete."

The devs go on to thank interested gamers for their support, enthusiasm and patience. It's an interesting delay, because just last month, game director Xiangyu Luo told Automaton that the "game's content is already completely finished" and that the team is now in the process of "polishing its overall quality." So a year for polish? I'm pleased the team has the resources for that kind of investment.

The most recent update we had from the game was at Gamescom Opening Night live (see above), back in August. Here, the developer revealed a bit more about the game's background and gameplay, showing off the Japanese voice cast for the first time. "Showa American Story follows the journey of Choko, a young woman who suddenly revives from the dead to discover a wild world filled with zombies, monsters, and an eccentric cast of human survivors - some friendly, and others downright bad," reads a blurb for that trailer.

"Players will travel across the United States in search of answers and discover the extent of Choko's mysterious and frightening powers. This unique RPG features a rich arsenal of melee and ranged weaponry, with Choko able to turn a variety of objects into tools of carnage. Choko will face hordes of enemies in fast-paced real-time combat, leveraging weapon-specific attacks, dodges, counters, and executions with fluid precision." In other words, you can expect a game that's pitched in a similar way to the Yakuza series, albeit from a greenhorn developer without the satirical nous.

#3632. Not upgrading to iPhone 18 Pro or Duo? Here’s what’s coming in 2027

iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Duo have been out for quite some time now, and despite that, it’s still incredibly challenging to order an iPhone Duo in a timely manner. If for whatever reason you’re considering skipping out on this year’s iPhones, here’s what you have to look forward to next year.

2027 is going to be a relatively big iPhone release year for Apple. First, the company will be continuing the iPhone 18 lineup after it introduced a split release schedule. Then, in the fall, the company will debut a new round of flagships in celebration of the 20th anniversary of the iPhone. Here’s what to expect.

For the first time, Apple will be introducing its base iPhone in the spring. Upgrades for the iPhone 18 aren’t quite clear, though more RAM is one of the key rumors. Thermal upgrades will likely happen as well, as well as the new Apple C2 modem.

It’s possible Apple will update the design to fall more in line with the iPhone 17 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro, though we don’t yet know.

This phone will of course equip the A20 chip, and it’ll probably start at the same $899 price point that iPhone 17 currently sits at – after it was increased from $799 in September.

This phone will most likely just end up being a chip bump from the A19 to A20 chip, and debut in the Spring alongside the iPhone 18. Earlier this year, reports indicated that Apple would share many components between the iPhone 18 and iPhone 18e, though it isn’t quite clear what that could mean for the devices.

Out of all of the spring iPhone releases, this one is the one to look forward to. After receiving a lukewarm reception with the initial iPhone Air model, Apple went back to the drawing board and decided to modify the design to fit an ultrawide camera into the device.

Personally, I don’t think an ultrawide camera is too important – though many people will see one camera on the back of the phone and immediately assume it’s less premium, so it’ll probably end up being an important upgrade for the sake of sales. Plus, ultrawide photos can be fun at times.

It should also have a larger battery, reportedly as large as 3500mAh. That’s a roughly 10% improvement from the original iPhone Air. iPhone Air 2 will likely also jump from Apples C1X modem to the C2.

For the 20th anniversary of the iPhone, Apple is expected to debut a fully redesigned iPhone to celebrate. It’ll reportedly be much more glassy, feature significantly slimmer bezels, a quad curved display, and ditch the flat edge design of the iPhone 12 and later.

Personally, I’m slightly skeptical that this’ll truly be a replacement to the “Pro” phone for thermal reasons, but time will tell. iPhone Duo seemingly has strong thermals while not featuring an aluminum unibody, so my concern might not be relevant. It’ll offer two, larger display sizes: 6.4-inch and 7-inch. This largely comes from the bezel reduction.

I wish they prioritized the Telephoto camera more. I need that (whether it be on an Air or a Duo) way more than an Ultrawide.

If you’re holding out for iPhone 18 Pro, this “iPhone 20” is definitely the phone to wait out for.

Lastly, Apple will release a successor to its just-announced iPhone Duo next fall. Of course, you can expect next-generation Apple Silicon with the A21 Pro chip next year, but there aren’t many other substantial changes expected. Apple may bring proper Face ID to the outer display, an improvement from the recently-announced face unlock, but it’s unclear whether this feature will make the engineering cutoff date.

#3631. CD Projekt Red signs new marketing partnership deal with Sony for The Witcher 4, and to increase "the presence" of its games on PlayStation

As part of The Witcher and Cyberpunk studio CD Projekt Red's recent Q3 earnings report, the developer offered some updates on upcoming game The Witcher 4.

During an earnings call yesterday, the studio revealed it had signed a new partnership deal with Sony regarding marketing rights to The Witcher 4, as well as to extend "the presence" of CD Projekt Red's other games across the PlayStation Store and PlayStation Plus.

"Just today, we signed new partnership agreements with Sony Interactive Entertainment covering the presence of our games on PlayStation and in PlayStation Plus subscriptions, as well as our collaboration during the upcoming Witcher 4 marketing campaign," said studio CFO Piotr Nielubowicz. "This cooperation will support our business and financial outlook in this and future years."

Nielubowicz didn't elaborate on what exactly that means for The Witcher 4's marketing, but perhaps it could enable Sony to advertise the action-RPG as a PlayStation game, similar to the Grand Theft Auto 6 'plays best on PlayStation' campaign. But seeing as The Witcher 4 is currently targeting a 2028 release, we may not find out what form that agreement takes for some time.

That said, looking at similar marketing agreements from Sony's recent history, we can probably expect The Witcher 4 to show up during Sony State of Play presentations or even have dedicated PlayStation-focused showcases. The Witcher 4 footage may also be specified as being captured on PlayStation hardware - something we already saw with The Witcher 4 tech demo last year. Perhaps we'll see Witcher-themed accessories and PlayStation hardware, too.

This is a notable shift for CDPR, which has historically had close ties to Xbox. Cyberpunk 2077's big Keanu Reeves reveal (as Johnny Silverhand) took place on Xbox's E3 2019 stage, and The Witcher 3's reveal happened on Microsoft's E3 2013 stage. Going further back, Xbox 360 was the only console The Witcher 2 was released on.

During the same earnings call, CDPR joint-CEO Michał Nowakowski said that we should expect the leap between The Witcher 3 and The Witcher 4 to be similar to that between GTA 5 and GTA 6, while also praising Rockstar's approach to marketing its record-breaking new game.

I'm a hardcore reality TV fan, and this year is my first time watching a full season of The Great British Baking Show with my Netflix subscription. While longtime fans have been criticizing its twists or coming after the way Nigella Lawson eats, I've had a total blast watching the heartwarming competition series. Although I will say I totally called out a problem from Day 1 that ended up having a big impact on the semifinals episode.

Following Connie's truly heartbreaking elimination, the semifinal episode of Bake Off featured the top four contestants creating Patisseries. There was just one big problem: the heat wave in the U.K. was making it especially hot in the iconic tent. Unfortunately that threw a wrench into the baker's plans, especially when they needed the time to cool their bakes. I thought this was going to be a big problem over the course of the season, and I feel totally vindicated after watching the semifinal episode of the season.

The struggle of cooling bakes has been a recurring theme throughout this season of Bake Off, and it had major implications during Patisserie week. This was especially true for the technical challenge, where contestants needed to create judge Paul Hollywood's Gateau Concorde in 21⁄2 hours. Inside the tent was reportedly a whopping 94 degrees, and a number of the bakes suffered as a result.

Unfortunately, Gabe struggled quite a bit during the semifinals, partially thanks to the heat and his bakes not being able to properly cool. He ended up being eliminated before the finals, but he wasn't the only one who had issues with the heat while trying to craft his patisseries. Frontrunner Tom's babas were also underproofed, so it was clear that the heat wave was affecting the whole cast. I can't imagine how it must have felt to be so hot while baking, especially because I also tend to overheat when experiencing anxiety.

There's just one episode for this season of The Great British Baking Show, so the pressure is on for the final there bakers to stick the landing and hopefully pull out a W. While fans across the pond already know who will take the prize, we here in the states will have to wait until Black Friday to stream the finale episode on Netflix. I'm especially curious to see if the U.K. heatwave from last summer continues to be a menace for the contestants during their final few bakes. Can't we get some better air conditioning in the Bake Off tent?

#3629. Players discover over 1,500 individual buildings you can enter in GTA 6, nearly 28% of all buildings on the map

One GTA 6 player has put in the legwork and found that a shocking number of buildings across Leonida are freely accessible.

Per a Reddit post by Aileos, 1,563 of the game's 5,588 buildings can be entered, coming in at 27.97 percent of structures in the game. Some of those are ones you'd expect of course: stores, banks, and the like. But plenty of them may surprise you. The next time you're walking across a neighbourhood, pick a house and just walk inside… in-game, of course.

A funny quirk with this discovery is its relation to previous leaks for Grand Theft Auto 6. Back in 2025 it was claimed that over 700 buildings can be freely entered in GTA 6, something that received ample doubt from those anticipating the Rockstar release. Take this comment from user Macklaviel: "There's a difference between proven true and not proven wrong yet. 700 interiors would be astonishingly good but it sets the expectations too high and it realistically will be way less than that."

Plenty of the best secrets in GTA 6 can be found off the beaten trail. Random drops of illicit goods can be found all over the place. So, if you're having a blast making your way through the game, take an hour or so just to wander around the place and take in the scenery.

If you are in the market for some help through the game, Eurogamer's GTA 6 walkthrough is a great source of helpful information. Likewise, our page on all the GTA 6 cheats is a great help for those in need.

The Bravado Banshee is another one of the cars you'll need to track down for Randy in GTA 6, but unlike the Pegassi Infernus, this one doesn't involve anything as dodgy as robbing a police lockup.

You can find this car inside the Sunrise Premium Autos showroom at the north tip of Southside, southwest of Pay 'N' Spray - Salton or east across the road from Ron Gas - Southside. This region is to the northeast of Hamlet.

There are two showrooms here, so make sure you have the right one, though the other does contain Pfister Growlers, in case you haven't gotten that car for Randy yet, either. Head inside to find the car—if you've played previous GTAs, you'll recognise it as a convertible with a white stripe down the middle. Hop inside, use the key cloner, and drive it through the glass.

Just remember to drive fast, and if the tracker starts to beep, speed up to stop it pinging your location to the cops. Delivering this one gets you 6,500k and a 5k condition bonus as usual if it's in good nick.

The United Video Game Workers-CWA union has released a report with details on the hardship fund it started in collaboration with Necrosoft Games earlier this year benefiting laid-off developers. The UVW reports that through its itch.io bundle and from monies received via union dues and outside donations, it raised $290,000 over two weeks. All that cash has been dispersed to over 150 devs from across the industry to help with expenses like rent, medical bills, and other debt.

"This came at a time when I deeply, deeply needed a hand to pull me up while I'm drowning."

Perusing the report’s list of studios from which applicants to the fund have been laid off is depressing. Among them are some of the biggest names in the industry: Xbox, Activision Blizzard, EA, Ubisoft, and more. It’s the human reckoning, the terrible price to all the industry upheaval that’s often glossed over in reports on resets, booming financials, and robust pipelines. The other equally sad detail is just how long many of these out-of-work people have worked in the industry, with 32 percent of applicants reporting 10 years or more.

The industry is experiencing a brain drain that will be incredibly difficult to recover from. Nintendo is able to make the games it can because it retains its employees, training them up to eventually lead games of their own. Jason Schreier reported at Bloomberg that 21 percent of Rockstar staff are vets with 10-plus years of experience, and they’ve just released what has the potential to be the best-selling, best-reviewed game of all time.

#3625. Blizzard is making a lot of the Diablo 4's event-specific Diablo 2 anniversary content permanent because everyone loved it in Season 15

Blizzard has officially unveiled Diablo 4's next live-service season: Season of Tyrael's Gambit. This is the ARPG's 16th season, and it follows on from the popular and well-received Season of Hell's Legacy.

In an unexpected move, Blizzard announced it's keeping some of the nostalgia-laiden content from the previous season, Season of Hell's Legacy, as a permanent addition. This is unusual, as the ephemeral nature of live seasons means new content goes away at the end of each season.

Season of Hell's Legacy paid tribute to Diablo's legacy and its 30th anniversary by introducing a lot of content inspired by previous Diablo games, chiefly Diablo 2. The list includes the return of iconic character Deckard Cain, a recreation of Old Tristram, and a big fight against the three Prime Evils - Diablo, Baal, and Mephisto - in their classic forms.

"We heard overwhelming requests for features from Season of Hell's Legacy to carry forward as permanent game features," Blizzard wrote in Season 16's announcement post. "While the entire season couldn't come along for the ride, we are implementing the following features with the launch of Season of Tyrael's Gambit that will carry forward in both Eternal and Seasonal realms."

Season of Tyrael's Gambit kicks off 1st December, so you still have time to access all of that in Diablo 4 until Season 15 ends. Certain things, such as craftable items, won't return, so you may as well try them while you can. That said, Blizzard is aware of the love some of those items have, and the developer said it may bring them back in the future.

For months, some fan favorites and newcomers alike at Warner Bros., New Line, Weta and even Hobbiton have been prepping for a brand new Lord of the Rings movie. Lips have been pretty tightly sealed about the new Hunt for Gollum project beyond the fact it’s set during the time shortly before the Fellowship of the Ring and will feature Andy Serkis both as director and Gollum himself. Returning cast members include Ian McKellen, Lee Pace and Elijah Wood stepping back into those Hobbit feet. Oh, and Jamie Dornan and Leo Woodall will provide some additional eye candy. (And good acting too, credit where credit is due!)

It’s hard to believe The Lord of The Rings: The Hunt For Gollum has already wrapped. The movie picked up principle photography in July of this year, and has been quietly chugging along for months, but it still feels like yesterday it was getting off the ground. This morning, Andy Serkis and co. revealed the movie has wrapped in a new post that has me champing at the bit to see what’s next.

The news comes just a few weeks after Jamie Dornan admitted he’d wrapped his own portion of the movie. (There may have been some crying involved.) For his part, Andy Serkis has shared his return in the mo-cap suit, and now we've gotten a taste at Gollum's return in this funny wrap video.

To note, I’m not the only one impressed by Serkis donning the mo-cap suit at 62, either.

Warner Bros. revealed the new franchise film will be returning to the Shire back in September, a fact I can also confirm thanks to a lovely visit to the set of the movie and Hobbiton, courtesy of the studio. The movie shot for several days on location in the real-life version of the Shire on the Alexander Farm before heading to the soundstage in New Zealand, and the end result should be nothing short of epic, but that will also mean there’s plenty to do in post ahead. The movie itself isn’t scheduled to hit theaters for over a year, but I’ll take any tidbit I can get in the meantime.

It’s been a great holiday season for Lord of the Rings fans already. Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power dropped its final two episodes for Season 3 this week, and Season 4 was announced! Now, we know the upcoming 2027 movie release is ready to go into post-production. It's a big week, but December 17th, 2027 couldn’t come soon enough.

#3622. GTA 6 recompilers and vibe-coders implore AI chatbots to 'work faster' and 'make no mistakes' as they race to get the game running on PC

Things continue to get messy in the community of players working on getting Grand Theft Auto 6 working on PC. The previous frontrunner, Project Leonida, got their Discord server and GitHub repository taken down by Rockstar, but others have seemingly stepped in to finish the job.

The most up-to-date build of GTA 6 was allegedly leaked earlier this week by notorious leaker CyberLeek. This is a supposedly near-final build of the game's Xbox version, and it's seemingly being used as the basis for the recent work to port the game to PC.

Unsurprisingly, most of these communities of modders rely almost exclusively on generative-AI tools like Claude and Antigravity to decompile and recompile the console version of GTA 6. That has always been the case, but the CyberLeek build only invited even more to ask AI chatbots to make the PC port for them.

X user chasm has been following developments in the GTA 6 decompile and recompile communities, and recently shared some of the prompts the so-called vibe-coders are using - a few of whom livestreamed the process.

"Make no mistakes," one modder prompted the AI chatbot. "Keep finding more stuff and working and pushing," another eloquently asked. "Work faster," asked another. "There has to be a faster way to iterate than this," they continued.

Rockstar, which successfully managed to DMCA take down Project Leonida - including all of its 3,006 forks on lead author NotRexed's GitHub - is seemingly also going after people online discussing the community's progress. The X user in question later revealed they may no longer be able to share these updates, as their posts have also been removed "in response to a report by the copyright owner".

As for how far some of the remaining communities have managed to get, this video allegedly shows the game running on PC. This goes beyond the boot-up screen, which modders were able to reach within hours of CyberLeek's build alleged leaking.

The footage runs at sub-5fps, but the visuals look to have rendered normally. Assuming Rockstar doesn't also shut down the modders who remain active, we may see another progress update.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

After two weeks of voting that bracketed the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6, Rockstar Games employees have voted overwhelmingly against a recognition agreement with the IWGB Game Workers Union.

25% of Rockstar employees voted in favor of the recognition agreement, the union said, while 75% voted against it. 1,544 employees took part in the vote, representing a turnout of just over 93%.

Rockstar workers actually founded a union earlier this year—the Rockstar Game Workers Union, a subsidiary of the Independent Workers Union of Great Britain—and it will continue to operate as it has. The IWGB said the outcome will not prevent Rockstar workers from organizing or exercising union rights, but the company will not be required to regularly meet with union representatives for collective bargaining or other relevant matters.

Despite the vote, the union said it will continue with organizing efforts at Rockstar.

"For anyone at Rockstar who believes in a fairer workplace, a fairer sector and a fairer society—this isn’t a sign to retreat, it’s a sign to double down on what we stand for. Hundreds of our coworkers voted in favour of our union at Rockstar, yet sadly we recognize we have more work to do to build understanding and win the trust of more of our colleagues," the IWGB Rockstar Game Workers Union said. "We’re ready to put in the effort to make that happen.

"Whilst we haven’t emerged with a recognition deal, this ballot has put our union on the radar of every worker, and opened the door for new kinds of conversation to start happening. People entirely unfamiliar with unions were for the first time debating employment conditions, collective bargaining rights, and our contracts. We heard from many more colleagues about what mattered to them, and we hope people will continue to engage so that we can see where these new discussions can lead us."

The power to shape our working lives has always been, and always will be, in our hands

In a separate statement, Rockstar head of publishing Jennfer Kolbe said the studio is "extraordinarily proud of our team, the culture we've built together and the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6."

"This result reflects our team's strong support for continuing the direct relationships, collaboration and open dialogue that have helped make Rockstar Games so innovative and strong," Kolbe said. "As we look ahead, we're excited to build on all we've accomplished together."

Rockstar, which said it worked with the IWGB to ensure employees were able to make an informed decision in a fair and transparent vote, came under fire in October 2025 for firing more than 30 employees, all of whom were members of a private trade union Discord channel. The IWGB called it "the most ruthless act of union busting in the history of the UK games industry," while Rockstar says they were fired for leaking information about "upcoming and unannounced games." That matter is now before an employment tribunal; closing submissions were made last week.

Amid the various changes that have unfolded at 60 Minutes under Bari Weiss’ leadership, a handful of staffers have remained in the fold. Veteran broadcaster Lesley Stahl is one of those people, as she chose to remain with the series alongside cohorts Bill Whitaker and Jon Wertheim. Up to this point, it seemed that Stahl and Weiss had been able to work together harmoniously. However, if a recent report is to be believed, Stahl is now taking issue with CBS News’ Editor-in-Chief for a major reason.

This reported situation apparently has to do with editorial autonomy on Stahl’s part. According to the Wall Street Journal (via The New York Post), Stahl is allegedly frustrated with Weiss and co. interfering with her reporting. The news outlet claims that one particular sticking point has to do with changes made to a story involving violence that Palestinians reportedly faced from Israeli settlers in the West Bank. That segment aired back in October after Stahl apparently objected to Charles Forelle, Weiss’ deputy E-I-C, holding it.

Per this reporting, much of the supposed displeasure on Stahl’s part also has to do with Weiss’ perceived lack of experience in the broadcast news industry. Before Skydance (then Paramount Skydance) chief David Ellison hired Weiss in October 2025, she’d founded the online outlet known as The Free Press. That organization was also acquired by Paramount around the same time Weiss was hired. If these claims about Stahl are true, she wouldn’t be the first to question Weiss’ leadership skills.

Another person who has spoken openly about Bari Weiss is former 60 Minutes correspondent, Scott Pelly, who was fired this past May after allegedly accusing the exec of "murdering" the show. Pelley spoke out about Weiss during a subsequent interview and cast doubt upon her ability to run the legacy news brand. It was Pelley’s assertion that the Eye Network was in need of some “adult supervision.”

Ex-60 Minutes EP On His Biggest Concerns Amid Bari Weiss’ Leadership: ‘That Would Have Freaked Me Out’

Pelley is also one of several former employees who have made claims of “journalistic interference” against the new leadership team at CBS News. He, Cecilia Vega and more have alleged that they were encouraged to insert what they believed to be news-related bias into their reporting. On the other side of this equation, Weiss and co. have denied presenting biased reporting. Some have also come to Weiss’ defense during this time, with CBS Evening News anchor Tony Dokoupil defending her vision and saying he hadn’t personally seen any instances of bias.

All of that aside, 60 Minutes reportedly finds itself in a tough situation, as the program has seen ratings-related setbacks amid Season 59. One of the latest reports makes note of the show having averaged 8.3 million viewers for its nine episodes that aired between September 9 and November 16. That marked a 16 percent decrease from the previous season. Ahead of that, Weiss addressed concerns about the show and said it had been doing “tremendously well.”

If the situation involving Lesley Stahl is legitimate, though, it would mark yet another behind-the-scenes issue for Bari Weiss. Said conflict would also theoretically add more pressure for Stahl, who’s been receiving backlash for having remained with the show now that Weiss and executive producer EP Nick Bilton are in charge. Time will tell whether any further developments arise in this matter.

#3617. World of Warcraft: Forever's best new enchantment has been quietly changed, leaving some casters on the back foot

As World of Warcraft: Forever players dived into the game, they quickly discovered a specific weapon enchant that took area of effect spells to a whole other level. Sadly, with a sudden hotfix last night, this particular use case for the enchant has been removed.

The enchantment in question was Revelation - a new addition to the game included as part of the new trade good reputations. What it does is simple: when you fail to deal a critical strike with a spell, the next spell hit is guaranteed to do so. What made this particularly powerful is that the buff also worked with continuous area of effect spells, meaning an early instance of the spell not crit-ing would result in the remaining damage hits all dealing critical damage.

So for example, let's say you're a druid casting the Hurricane spell. This is a channel spell with a total of 10 seconds of cast time. Every second, it deals damage. If the first instance of damage at the one second mark doesn't crit, the remaining nine instances of damage would all crit. This resulted in absurd amounts of damage, and made players of druids, warlocks, and mages very happy.

While strong enchantments are often pricey, this was notably cheap, due to the low-cost of resources used to create it and the low requirements to learn it. As such, people were spending a handful of gold for an early game enchantment that was being actively used all the way into the end game.

It was admittedly a tad too strong, and the effect triggered on AOE spells was almost certainly an unintended effect of the enchantment. Last night, the fun came to an end. Now, the effect is used up as intended in long-casted spells. So going back to the example given, if the first instance of damage on Hurricane doesn't crit, then the second one still will. However, this will use up the effect, and the third instance of damage will revert to regular ol' damage numbers. It also seems as though it Revelation can't trigger more than once during a single channeled spell.

This is the latest in a string of ongoing quickfire bug fixes and game adjustments being made to World of Warcraft: Forever. The devs have been continuously updating the game in an attempt to curb certain gold farms, following the discovery of a particularly lucrative Blackmaw Hold gold exploit. The dev team has expressed some interesting ideas for the game longterm, including a desire to kill best-in-slot gear.

#3616. GTA 6 Boss Reveals How That Very Surprising Cameo Happened And What It Means For The Character

Grand Theft Auto 6GTA 6Rob NelsonRockstar Games

Grand Theft Auto 6Â contains a surprising but cool cameo hidden near the very end of the game’s main story. So when I got a chance to chat with Rockstar’s head of production, Rob Nelson, about GTA 6 ahead of the game’s launch, I had to ask about this moment, how it came about, and what it means for the character.

But uh… major spoilers. Seriously, if you’re a big GTA nerd and love to be surprised, turn around right now and stop reading. You’ll thank me later when you reach this point and get to experience it unspoiled. For those who don’t care or who can’t resist the siren’s call of secrets being revealed, keep scrolling past the warning. Just don’t yell at me later!

As you approach the final missions in the game, Jason and Lucia start working with Giorgio, a very rich shipping magnate who works with Eastern European criminals to smuggle drugs across the ocean on his big ships. And things aren’t going well, forcing Giorgio to work with Jason, Lucia, and others on a big, ambitious plan to steal back all the cocaine confiscated by the Coast Guard as part of a large heist. But before they can pull off the heist, a higher-up from the big Balkan cartel Giorgio has been working with arrives to kill him for screwing up, but gives him one more chance to get back the coke. That badass hitman? Niko Bellic, the playable protagonist of 2008’s Grand Theft Auto IV.

Here’s the scene from GTA 6 in which he appears:

I asked Nelson if they’d planned to include Niko from the start, and he tells me that they hadn’t. Instead, he told me that the cameo came about “very organically.”

“[Early in development], we had Giorgio and we had him working with a sort of Balkan cartel,” explained Nelson. The GTA 6 boss further explained that this whole storyline was based on research they’d done about actual Italian shipping companies that allegedly smuggled drugs for various gangs in South America. Apparently, a boat run by such a company was carrying 20 tons of coke when it was raided by U.S. officials. That number should sound familiar to anyone who has played the later missions of GTA 6, as that’s the amount of coke seized by the Coast Guard in the game.Â

“Giorgio is not really a criminal. He’s a sort of wealthy shipping magnate who’s in league with these criminals,” said Nelson.

“But it was sort of that same [real-world] idea. And then we needed someone from the Balkan cartel to show up. It just grew very organically, and it’s like, well, who would he be working with from the Balkan end of the organization? When Giorgio fucks up, who’s going to come down to deal with him? And I got an idea.”

Nelson says Niko’s story was sort of “left open” after the events of GTA IV.Â “He’s still kicking around. He’s still in play,” he told Kotaku. Nelson also confirmed original voice actor Michael Holick returned for the role. When I asked if it was nice to have him back and work with him again, Nelson responded with a smile: “Very much, yeah.”Â

I asked Nelson if this cameo confirms anything about which ending is canon in GTA IV, and Nelson wouldn’t say one way or the other and pointed out that nothing Niko says or does in either cutscene indicates a specific canon ending for that game. He did confirm that Niko will be going back to Liberty City after all this and that it’s been his home since GTA IV.Â

There’s one more great detail included in this cameo moment. After the cutscene ends, players hear the mission-complete jingle from GTA IV play instead of one of GTA 6‘s various mission-complete jingles. According to Nelson, that was a “late addition.”

“For a long time it was like a normal [GTA 6] stinger, and we played it and…” Nelson made an meh face. “I got on with Yvonne and said, ‘Can we put the [mimics the GTA IV mission complete jingle] in there?'” And they did, which was a wonderful touch to an already amazing moment.Â

When we talked about Niko Bellic in GTA 6, Nelson did admit that he hoped “it stays secret for a bit.” Sadly, a lot of people rushed through GTA 6 and posted videos of Niko last week, less than three days after the game’s launch. Welp.
